scope: Read-only provenance review; no live case or solver inputs modified.

runtime.runner_order: Four manifests, including processor-inputs.sha256, are verified before GO; then RUN_RELEASED_UTC is written and mpirun is executed. Runner contains no T.air/T.water normalizer.

seed.comparison: Parent seed exactly matches frozen phase-field hashes. Both stage files were overwritten about 0.69 s after release; common T kept its hash. This is post-GO solver activity, not a wrong initial copy or quota edit.

array_checks.scope: Binary decomposedBlockData, all 10 processor pieces, 299214 internal cells and physical open-patch values.
array_checks.interpretation: After startup, both phase-field internal arrays equal common T to roundoff and their open-patch boundary arrays exactly equal common T. Before startup, these three physical patch lists were empty. The scalar64 payload accounts for nearly all growth; the remaining 210 bytes per file is file serialization/layout.

source_trace.operations: Copies T_ into T1/T2 (T.air/T.water), writes both, flushes, constructs phase rhoThermo objects that read those files, then calls correct().
source_trace.meaning: The phase fields are solver-generated and computationally active startup derivatives of common T, not independently prescribed physical initial temperatures. This comparison does not claim behavior after subsequent timesteps.

conclusion.cause: The frozen phase fields passed pre-GO checks and matched the immutable parent. The OpenFOAM twoPhaseMixtureThermo constructor rewrote them after GO from common T and materialized boundary values.
conclusion.future_recording: Keep pre-GO manifest immutable and valid; record constructor-generated hashes separately or label phase T as derived startup outputs. Do not add a shell normalizer. At later restarts, freeze the actual checkpoint files before the runner checks them.
